default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1378.title: Bollinger band re-entry fade
E-1378.hypothesis: A close beyond k standard deviations of the recent closes and back inside next bar is an overshoot that liquidity providers absorb; fade it back to the mean.

E-1379.title: Session-open price recross follow
E-1379.hypothesis: After price held one side of the session open for a while, a close across it shows buyers or sellers who defended the open have given up; follow the cross.

E-1380.title: Round-number rejection
E-1380.hypothesis: Round index levels hold resting orders; a bar that touches the level and closes back away from it with its body shows those orders absorbed the push; fade.

E-1381.title: Volume-spike climax bar fade
E-1381.hypothesis: A bar with volume far above normal for the time that closes at its extreme against the body direction is a climax: late aggressors are trapped; fade it.

E-1382.title: Narrowest-range bar breakout
E-1382.hypothesis: The narrowest bar of the last n bars marks compression; a close beyond its high or low releases the stored energy in that direction.

E-1383.title: Bar-open gap fade
E-1383.hypothesis: A bar opening far from the previous close (relative to the usual bar range) is a thin-book jump; if the bar closes back toward the previous close the jump is being retraced; fade it.

E-1384.title: Volatility-expansion direction follow
E-1384.hypothesis: When short-term volatility jumps above the longer-term level, a regime of directional order flow starts; follow the direction of the short window.

E-1385.title: Extreme streak exhaustion reversal
E-1385.hypothesis: After m consecutive bars each making a new lower low (higher high), a bar closing beyond the previous bar's opposite extreme shows the pressure is spent; trade the reversal.

E-1386.title: Fast-slow EMA cross follow
E-1386.hypothesis: A fast EMA crossing a slower one (3x) marks a change in the recent drift that slower participants chase; follow the cross.

E-1387.title: Closing-extreme break on heavy bars
E-1387.hypothesis: A close beyond every close of the last n minutes on above-average volume is a break with participation rather than a thin poke; follow it.
